ai.description: This gecko reaches 50 mm in snout-vent length. It is brownish-grey with dark dorsal blotches and a white venter. It is distinguished by its lack of a distinct precloacal pore arrangement.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus kolliensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a single internasal scale separating the nostrils, whereas most similar Indian species possess two.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus kolliensis* is endemic to the Kolli Hills of the Eastern Ghats, inhabiting moist deciduous forests and rocky outcrops at altitudes between 1,000–1,300 meters.
ai.behavior: The Kolli Rock Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects on rocky outcrops and tree trunks within its restricted habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus kolliensis* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus kolliensis* is endemic to the Kolli Hills in the Eastern Ghats of Tamil Nadu, India, typically inhabiting rocky outcrops at elevations above 1,000 meters.
